{{Quote|We'd hit the alien digs most. Swokes Swokes and Duros can never fig how old humans really are, so we'd get in without ever getting scanned.|[[Pori Nate]], on obtaining [[Death stick/Legends|death sticks]]|<ref name="DSS">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|49|life/13328_1.html|SPECIAL REPORT: The Death Stick Scourge}}</ref>}}
The '''Swokes Swokes''' were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] native to the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Makem Te/Legends|Makem Te]]. Large, stocky creatures, they had sharp, protruding [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]], perpetually grinning [[Mouth/Legends|mouths]], a series of horns crowning their pallid heads, one to three [[Nose/Legends|nostrils]], and no [[Hair/Legends|hair]]. Some members of the species had long, heavy, spiked tails. Swokes Swokes had the ability to regenerate lost body parts, an ability that afforded them considerable bravado on the battlefield. [[Death/Legends|Death]] was a prominent aspect of their culture; indeed, the [[Tract of Makem Te|Tract]] was an enormous expanse of tombs and crypts on their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] that supported a major part of the planetary economy and was visible from [[Realspace/Legends|space]]. The Swokes Swokes viewed jewelry as a status symbol and often had [[Gemstone/Legends|gems]] implanted close to vital organs. Most Swokes Swokes were religious zealots. Makem Te society had little advanced technology. Builders relied on sturdy yet delicate-looking cast [[Iron/Legends|iron]] for their primary construction material, and transport often relied on domesticated serpentine creatures called [[schinga]]s.

A coalition of royal families known as the [[Congress of Caliphs]] ruled the species' homeworld. The planet and its natives escaped widespread attention from [[The galaxy/Legends|the greater galaxy]] until [[Scientist/Legends|scientists]] from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] discovered rich veins of [[Ore/Legends|ore]] and [[Spice/Legends|spice]] on the world and brokered a [[Mining/Legends|mining]] deal with the planetary government. The introduction of galactic technology set off a wave of social unrest on Makem Te, disturbing the tradition-minded people and spurring several religious schisms. The [[Temple of the Beatific Razor]], a violence-worshiping sect, attracted enough adherents to challenge the authority of the aristocracy. Over the next few decades, the caliphs called in the aid of a succession of multi-system governments as their allegiances swung from one political pole to another: first the Galactic Republic&mdash;a body in which the species was represented at the time of the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]]&mdash;then the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], and finally the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. The Swokes Swokes never joined the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], although they did establish relations with the [[New Jedi Order]].

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:Gragra_full_body_3-4_shot.png|thumb|left|upright|Not all Swokes Swokes had tails.]]
{{Quote|Regenerate ''that''!|Jedi Knight Toro Irana upon beheading a Swokes Swokes opponent|<ref name="Scourge" />}}
The Swokes Swokes were large,<ref name="Scourge" /> stocky, [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] bipeds who stood between 1.4 and 2 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall.<ref name="Geonosis" /> They had four or five clawed fingers on each massive [[Limb/Legends|hand]],<ref>''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]'' states that Swokes Swokes have four fingers per hand, yet ''[[The Bounty Hunters: Aurra Sing]]'' depicts one with five.</ref><ref name="TPM" /> which enabled them to effect a firm but soft grip.<ref name="Scourge" /> Four forward-pointing toes on each foot were balanced by a single backward-facing digit.<ref name="FF GOR2">{{FactFile|89|GOR 1-2|Gragra the Gorgmonger}}</ref> The beings had long, thick tails that ended in knobby spikes, although not all members of the species exhibited this trait.<ref name="WOS" /><ref name="FF GOR2" /> Their glistening,<ref name="Geonosis" /> [[Hair/Legends|hairless]]<ref name="FF GOR2" /> loose-hanging<ref name="CSWE III 202">{{CSWECite|III|202|Swokes Swokes}}</ref> skin covered their rolls of fat, which made striking a member of the species feel like hitting soft dough.<ref name="Scourge" /> The skin ranged in [[Color/Legends|color]] from sallow gray to ashen off-white,<ref name="Geonosis" /><ref name="Best Birthday Ever">"[[Best Birthday Ever]]" shows a pink-skinned Swokes Swokes, but this is a non-[[canon]]ical source.</ref> and their soft tissue was thick and rubbery.<ref name="Geonosis" />

The Swokes Swokes visage was primarily flat<ref name="Scourge" /> and featured two large, lidless [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] that ranged from black to red,<ref name="Geonosis" /><ref name="WOS" /><ref name="Hasbro" /> blue,<ref name="AS" /> or white set into black sockets<ref name="Scourge" /> and hidden behind goggle-like natural shades.<ref name="FF GOR2" /> A gaping [[Mouth/Legends|grin]] of irregular, fang-like [[Tooth/Legends|incisors]]<ref name="BHP">''[[The Clone Wars: Secret Missions 2: Curse of the Black Hole Pirates]]''</ref><ref name="Geonosis" />&mdash;unable to form a frown<ref name="Scourge" />&mdash;and one to three [[Nose/Legends|nostrils]] lie beneath.<ref>All Swokes Swokes in the ''Star Wars'' films have three nostrils; however, ''[[The Bounty Hunters: Aurra Sing]]'' depicts individuals with one and two nostrils, and the Prologue of [[Scourge (novel)|''Scourge'']] calls the number "random."</ref> The bulbous head<ref name="CSWE III 202" /> was situated atop the fleshy neck,<ref name="BHP" /> although the neck itself was hidden under folds of flesh.<ref name="Scourge" /> The head was ringed by a series of sharp horns, and another set of horns at the top.<ref name="CSWE III 202" /> To non-Swokes Swokes, the overall appearance was almost humorous or at the very least unattractive,<ref name="Scourge" /> but was often thought more akin to that of a creature common to the nightmares of many cultures.<ref name="Geonosis" />

Internally, Swokes Swokes biology resembled that of more primitive lifeforms, such as [[flatworm]]s. The species' [[nervous system]] was underdeveloped in comparison to other sentients, lacking all but the most essential pain receptors. This gave the beings a remarkably high pain threshold but deadened their sense of touch. Swokes Swokes [[Blood/Legends|blood]] had the consistency of [[Water/Legends|watery]] [[Sap/Legends|sap]] and oozed through their bodies. Like flatworms, they had the ability to regenerate lost body parts,<ref name="Geonosis" /> although the process left scars.<ref name="Scourge" /> Regrowing a missing limb took about 10 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|standard days]], provided the individual avoided physical exertion.<ref name="Geonosis" /> Swokes Swokes could not regenerate a head, so beheading killed them instantly.<ref name="Scourge" /> Nevertheless, coupled with their naturally damage-resistant hides and resistance to pain, their regenerative properties made Swokes Swokes fierce, relentless opponents in battle.<ref name="Geonosis" /> Despite their unique internal physiology, Swokes Swokes were susceptible to certain forms of [[Spice/Legends|spice]], including [[Tempest (spice)|Tempest]]. Once addicted, they were immune to the physical pain of withdrawal, although they suffered psychological effects during such abstention. The species was divided into two [[Gender/Legends|sexes]]: male<ref name="Scourge" /> and female.<ref name="FF GOR1">{{FactFile|89|GOR 1-2|Gragra the Gorgmonger}}</ref>

Swokes Swokes entered adolescence at 9 standard years and were considered adults at 14 standard years. An average member of the species lived to 75 standard years. Swokes Swokes grew tougher and more resilient with age. The oldest were often the most difficult to take down in a fight.<ref name="Geonosis" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|Where'd you learn to speak Swoken?''"''<br />''"''A friend from Makem Te.''"''<br />''"''What I wouldn't give to see Makem Te again.|Mokshok and Lalo Gunn|<ref name="BHP" />}}
[[File:SwokesSwokesPirate-AurraSing.jpg|thumb|right|Swokes Swokes were known as brutes and bullies.]]
The Swokes Swokes had a reputation as merciless, unscrupulous, overbearing ruffians who cared only for personal prestige. This desire manifested differently from being to being, with some Swokes Swokes guided by mercurial longing for money and others more concerned for fame, notoriety, or influence over others. The view of the Swokes Swokes as brutes was reinforced by official Swokes Swokes institutions and religious doctrines. Wealth was one measure of status, and expensive gifts were a sure way to gain an audience with a Swokes Swokes. A popular status symbol was to have [[Gemstone/Legends|gemstones]] surgically embedded in the flesh near vital organs. The practice became so common that [[Bioscan/Legends|bioscanners]] operated in most Swokes Swokes buildings so that the relative status of the individuals inside could be detected and monitored; this practice prevented all but the most determined Swokes Swokes from trying to pass themselves off as coming from a higher station than their own.<ref name="Geonosis" />

Although not graceful creatures,<ref name="Scourge" /> Swokes Swokes were known for their fierceness in battle and their violent culture. The beings seemed made to fight, what with their resistance to pain, ability to regenerate lost limbs, natural weapons, and belligerent mindset;<ref name="Geonosis" /> when injured in battle, members of the species might cry out, but such a reaction was due to surprise or shock rather than pain.<ref name="Scourge" /> Swokes Swokes relished conservatism and the past. Ancient traditions guided the people for millennia, and the species disliked change. The most visible manifestation of this penchant was in Swokes Swokes religious beliefs.<ref name="Geonosis" />

The standard Swokes Swokes diet consisted of food and drink such as spiced, boiled meats served with [[schinga]] scales and still-living [[sandbug]]s; broiled [[Beetle/Legends|beetles]]; [[Alcohol/Legends|alcoholic]] [[scentwine]] served in double-handled mugs; [[Muja fruit/Legends|muja fruit]]; and [[Necrotic sugar candy|necrotic sugar candies]] shaped like the [[Bone/Legends|skulls]] of various species.<ref name="Scourge" /> They generally ate by sitting on [[Iron/Legends|iron]] stools and eating with [[Fork/Legends|forks]] from communal troughs, which ran the length of the table; still, at least some Swokes Swokes [[Restaurant/Legends|restaurants]] featured standard tables for patrons of other species. Swokes Swokes preferred cool temperatures and kept their businesses cold. Likewise, some Swokes Swokes made their living as [[Waiter/Legends|waiters]] in these establishments. They were loud and messy eaters, and they cared little for oral hygiene.<ref name="Scourge" /> [[Cannibalism]] was an acceptable punishment for disgraced members of the species and came in varying degrees of severity: to be eaten by one's own family members was preferable to being eaten by strangers.<ref name="DB Dokes">{{DB|character|oakiedokes|Dokes, Oakie}}</ref>

The Swokes Swokes' [[Language/Legends|language]] was known as [[Swoken]]. Other species found the language harsh and guttural,<ref name="BHP" /> or shrieking when Swokes Swokes got into disagreements.<ref name="Scourge" /> Written Swoken used a primitive [[Writing/Legends|alphabet]].<ref name="Geonosis" /> Members of the species sighed to convey forlorn feelings and laughed to convey amusement.<ref name="BHP" /> Most Swokes Swokes could speak and read [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]] as well,<ref name="Geonosis" /> although their voices sounded slurred and gurgling to outsiders when using that language. Likewise, Basic sounded unattractive and overly fluid to Swokes Swokes sensibilities.<ref name="Scourge" /> Some Swokes Swokes names were simple, such as Machug and Sorpaat. Others names commonly consisted of a given name followed by one other element. For some, this was a region of origin or a notable feature. Examples include [[Burba]] of Strekk and Fabswa the Mutilated.<ref name="Geonosis" /> Other Swokes Swokes had two different names, such as Oakie Dokes.<ref name="AOTC">{{Film|II}}</ref> Notable Swokes Swokes adopted a double name as a symbol of their fame. Examples included Woorta Woorta,<ref name="Geonosis" /> Yeb Yeb Adem'thorn,<ref name="TPM" /> Chako Chako, Gragra, Kruke Kruke, and Wruuta Wruuta.<ref name="Geonosis" />

===Institutions===
{{Quote|Diplomats? What an amazing coincidence! My first mate, Mokshok, used to be a diplomat. He was an ambassador of Makem Te. From what I've heard, he was a good one, too, not that he enjoyed it very much. Endless conferences and private meetings. Too many customs to remember. Always having to dress properly. But look at him now!|Hethra Mcgrrrr|<ref name="BHP" />}}
The [[Congress of Caliphs]], a body made up of hereditary family leaders, ruled the two billion Swokes Swokes of [[Makem Te/Legends|Makem Te]], the species' [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]]. Individual caliphs had sovereignty over individual [[City/Legends|settlements]] or portions of a larger population center. For example, 12 caliphs shared sovereignty over [[Thousand Thousand]], the largest city on the planet with its some two million inhabitants. The caliphs often hired Swokes Swokes or offworlders to do various services, especially if such job seekers brought appropriate offerings.<ref name="Geonosis" /> Makem Te dispatched [[Ambassador/Legends|ambassadors]] and [[Diplomat/Legends|diplomats]] to other worlds; such individuals had to attend innumerable conferences, uphold protocol, and wear specialized dress.<ref name="BHP" />

[[File:MakemTe_TheTract.jpg|thumb|left|upright|The Tract of Makem Te|Tract was a visual manifestation of the importance of religion in Swokes Swokes society.]]
Confrontations between Swokes Swokes often centered on religious disagreements.<ref name="Scourge" /> Indeed, rival religious sects vied for the devotion of the people. The most prominent of these was the [[Temple of the Beatific Razor]]. Its doctrines stressed fanatical devotion and the use of force against those who violated the order's precepts. Some Razor penitents flayed large strips of flesh from their bodies as a sign of their devoutness; such individuals appeared thinner than most Swokes Swokes. The Temple was ruled by 11 [[Temple of the Beatific Razor|High Mystics]]. Its radical policies, violent protests, and ever-growing popularity led to its banning by the Council of Caliphs.<ref name="Geonosis" />

Regardless of their sect, most Swokes Swokes believed in the veneration of their ancestors.<ref name="Geonosis" /> [[Funeral/Legends|Funeral]] planning was an artform in Swokes Swokes culture, and the dead were either buried or cremated. The [[Death/Legends|death]] of a high-status Swokes Swokes carried with it a mandatory mourning period at the place where the individual died.<ref name="Scourge" /> Swokes Swokes carried relics of their deceased relatives&mdash;their ashes or small body parts such as fingers, gallstones, or teeth&mdash;in small pouches.<ref name="Geonosis" /> These were considered good luck charms. This zealous devoutness was most readily apparent in the [[Tract of Makem Te|Tract]], an enormous patch of one of the planet's continents made up of two-meter-wide squares of polished stone,<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> each housing a monument called a ''[[stela]]''. Each tile was thought to contain the soul of a deceased Swokes Swokes. When [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] [[Scout/Legends|scouts]] discovered Makem Te some 25,000 to 24,000 years before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], the Tract had already reached 2,300 [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] on a side.<ref name="Geonosis" /> By the time of the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]], the Tract was home to more than 1.2 trillion stela and took up 7% of Makem Te's landmass.<ref name="CSWE II 278">{{CSWECite|II|278|Makem Te}}</ref> The Tract appeared as a large, white mass from [[Realspace/Legends|space]]; indeed, when Republic scouts first saw it from space, they mistook it for a polar icecap. The Tract was listed among the [[Wonders of the Galaxy/Legends|Twenty Wonders of the Galaxy]].<ref name="Geonosis" />

The Tract was of such importance to the Swokes Swokes that it supported its own industry. The maintenance of the area and its continued expansion required vast outflows of capital and a large workforce. This was overseen by the [[Tract Conviction]]. Record-keeping and accounting alone required millions of Conviction employees. Other Swokes Swokes, known as [[flatstender]]s, traveled the Tract in [[Landspeeder/Legends|landspeeders]], looking for areas in need of repair or for supplicants in need of help. Tract stones came from rock quarries. Flying over the Tract or traveling its expanse in vehicles was verboten and met with force from Makem Te defenses.<ref name="Geonosis" /> Instead, supplicants were expected to enter only at specified points, register with the Conviction, and pay a fee of up to 500 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]]. This covered the necessary sacraments, including a spotted [[Robe/Legends|robe]] of a color that signified which portions of the Tract the supplicant had the right to access. Even with flatstenders on guard, visitors still fell prey to desert hazards or attacks by wild creatures known as schingas. Offworlders faced the additional threat from penitents of the Beatific Razor, who considered visits by non-Swokes Swokes sacrilege and attacked such interlopers.<ref name="Geonosis" /> Settlements near the Tract catered to pilgrims with restaurants, [[Tapcafe/Legends|tapcafes]],<ref name="Scourge" /> and shops that sold funeral goods.<ref name="Scourge" />

===Trade and technology===
[[File:Schinga_Shikou_Rider.jpg|thumb|right|upright|The Swokes Swokes domesticated the schinga shikou for use as a mount.]]
{{Quote|Hey! Hey! Are you going to pay for that? It costs seven wupiupi.|translated=1|Gragra|<ref name="TPM" />}}
Although the Swokes Swokes had access to only primitive technology before contact with the Galactic Republic, they perfected the industries of metal working and animal husbandry. For centuries, Swokes Swokes cities were made of cast iron,<ref name="Geonosis" /> although by the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], this material was supplemented by [[Wood/Legends|wood]] as well as by plate [[Glass/Legends|glass]] for [[Window/Legends|windows]].<ref name="Scourge" /> This building strategy was originally a survival mechanism to withstand the constant wars on the planet, yet Swokes Swokes [[Metalsmith/Legends|smiths]] embraced the material and developed it to new heights of aesthetics. While such a material might have proved clumsy or unworkable to some species, Swokes Swokes smiths learned to create buildings and structures with intricate, even delicate, designs,<ref name="Geonosis" /> constructing structures such as spiral staircases from the material. They practiced recycling as well.<ref name="Scourge" />

The funeral industry was highly developed on Makem Te; practitioners of the funeral trade took great pride in their expertise, and one of the few situations in which a Swokes Swokes might prove helpful and friendly to an outsider was when planning for the interment or cremation of the deceased. Indeed, Swokes Swokes settlements sported large bazaars and marketplaces served by myriad alleyways.<ref name="Scourge" /> Vendors specialized in various items necessary for that sector of the planet's economy; these vendors sold such items as metal memorials, robes, funeral wrappings, tapestries, mementos, ointments, and wreaths. Warehouses supplied these salesbeings with wares. Meanwhile, [[Seer (profession)|seers]] and [[spiritualist]]s offered to contact the spirits of the newly deceased for family members worried about the adequacy of recently conducted funeral ceremonies. Alchemical shops also serviced the cities.<ref name="Scourge" />

The Swokes Swokes domesticated species of the serpent-like schinga, the dominant lifeform on Makem Te. For example, the [[schinga equa]] was used for its strength and obedience, while the [[schinga shikou]] was the most conducive to riding. To ride a schinga, the Swokes Swokes developed equipment known as a [[coiling tack]] set: a bit, bridle, reins, and saddle. A long [[Electropole/Legends|electropole]] was used to guide the schinga&mdash;and as an impromptu weapon in the event of an attack. Schinga shikou breeding was an important industry on Makem Te; the creatures were pricey signs of status.<ref name="Geonosis" />

Makem Te lay along the [[Perlemian Trade Route/Legends|Perlemian Trade Route]] and enjoyed a steady flow of space traffic. Hundreds of [[mining machine]]s operated on the planet. Although the machines were owned by offworld interests, a cut of the profits from the [[Ore/Legends|ores]] and spices extracted went to the Council of Caliphs. The mining machines were common targets for the Temple of the Beatific Razor, which opposed foreign influences on Makem Te. Major exports from Makem Te included raw ores and spices, while major imports were food and high technology.<ref name="Geonosis" />

==History==
{{Quote|Yellow star: Makem. Third planet: Makem Te. Arid, pebbly, no oceans, one large ice cap.|Republic scout|<ref name="Geonosis" />}}
The Swokes Swokes evolved on Makem Te, a desert world in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="Geonosis" /> The species' ancestors evolved thick hides to resist either fierce predators or severe radiation.<ref name="FF GOR2" /> With no surface water to drink, they learned to dig into the planet's subterranean aquifers, which were replenished by heavy rains twice each local year. A number of families rose to prominence and came to dominate the rest of the species. The heads of these families, known as caliphs, waged war on one another for generations. Under this constant onslaught of rival armies, Swokes Swokes turned to cast iron for a building material for its sturdiness. At some point before or shortly after the Galactic Republic discovered their world, the Swokes Swokes royalty joined forces to form the Congress of Caliphs, a governing body with planetwide jurisdiction. The Swokes Swokes developed a native religion based on ancestor worship. Religion joined warfare at the pinnacle of Swokes Swokes endeavor, and a planetwide graveyard known as the Tract began to take shape from an early date.<ref name="Geonosis" />

Between [[25,127 BBY|25,127]] and [[25,096 BBY]], strangers explored the areas of realspace in Makem Te's neighborhood. They belonged to the forces of [[Xim/Legends|Xim the Despot]], and before long, the Swokes Swokes' home [[Star system/Legends|system]] had fallen within the bounds of [[Xim's empire]]. Despite Xim's death around [[25,100 BBY]], Makem Te became part of a region of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] known to both the [[Tionese (group)/Legends|Tionese]] and the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]].<ref name="TEA" />

Sometime between [[15,000 BBY/Legends|15,000]] and [[10,000 BBY]],<ref name="TEA" /> a Republic scout visited the [[Makem system]] while mapping the [[Perlemian Trade Route/Legends|Perlemian Trade Route]]. The explorer made little note of Makem Te and even mistook the Tract for an ice cap. The scout's report made no mention at all of the Swokes Swokes. Long after the discovery, a Republic beacon crew came to install a [[Navigation buoy/Legends|navigation buoy]] in the system. Intrigued by Makem Te's large supposed ice cap, the mission sent a team of [[Scientist/Legends|scientists]] to visit the surface. There, they learned of the Tract's true nature and made contact with the Swokes Swokes. At this point the Tract had already sprawled to 2,300 kilometers on a side. The scientists entered the Swokes Swokes' iron cities and learned more about the planet and its lifeforms.<ref name="Geonosis" /> As news of the species and their world spread, the historian [[Vicendi]] included the Tract on his list of the [[Twenty Wonders of the Galaxy]] in 10,000 BBY.<ref name="TEA" /> Makem Te eventually became part of the [[Nilgaard sector/Legends|Nilgaard sector]].<ref name="EAOC">''[[Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion]]''</ref>

[[File:Yeb_yeb.jpg|thumb|left|Yeb Yeb Adem'thorn served as Makem Te's Senator in the Galactic Republic at the time of the Invasion of Naboo.]]
Although Makem Te joined the Republic at some point before the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]],<ref name="TPM" /> the Swokes Swokes and their planet were little more than a passing interest in the early days of their contacts with the galaxy at large. The Republic installed a [[Makem Te fueling station|fueling station]] in [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] around Makem Te and left the world largely to its own devices.<ref name="Geonosis" /> Nevertheless, over the centuries, the Swokes Swokes and their homeworld were caught up in galaxy-spanning conflicts. During the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]], the [[Dark Reaper campaign]] passed through their system and the [[Sith Empire (Exar Kun)/Legends|Sith Empire]] scored a victory there. Years later, the [[Mandalorian Wars]] saw [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] and Republic forces [[Battle of the Makem system (Mandalorian Wars)|clash]] in the system, an encounter that resulted in a Mandalorian victory. Later, their world fell within [[Revan/Legends|Darth Revan's]] [[Darth Revan's Sith Empire|Sith Empire]] during the [[Jedi Civil War]] from at least [[3959 BBY|3959]] to [[3956 BBY]].<ref name="TEA" />

Eventually, a pair of bored geologists, stuck at the Makem Te orbiting station for a long period, visited the surface and investigated one of the quarries where Tract stones were obtained. What they saw astounded them: Makem Te housed rich deposits of metal ores and medicinal spices. News of the discovery spread, and soon, Republic investors struck a deal with the Congress of Caliphs to allow them to establish [[Mining/Legends|mining]] operations on the world. Offworlders and advanced technology quickly became common sights on the planet and profoundly affected Swokes Swokes society. The [[Miner/Legends|miners]] paid little heed to environmental safeties, and the already harsh biosphere of Makem Te became even more inhospitable. As a people comfortable with ancient traditions, the infusion of foreign influences made some Swokes Swokes question their ages-old faith and institutions. Religious sects sprung up across the planet. One of these was the Temple of the Beatific Razor, which preached a faith of blind religious fervor and violent protest. As the Razor's popularity grew, the Temple's 11 High Mystics and swelling ranks of penitents gained enough influence to challenge the primacy of the Congress of Caliphs. The planetary government responded by calling in the aid of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] [[Judicial Department/Legends|Judicial Department]]. Security officers were dispatched to quell the Razor-led rebellions, pleasing the caliphs. but outraging the populace and driving more adherents to the Razor's cause.<ref name="Geonosis" />

After the outbreak of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the Beatific Razor eliminated all Republic peacekeepers on the planet. The galactic government, already taxed from waging the Clone Wars, abandoned its mission. Seeing little choice, the caliphs approached [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] for help in quelling the Razor's aggression's. Troops from the Separatist-allied [[Techno Union/Legends|Techno Union]] undertook the task of repelling the Razor penitents and propping up the caliphs. These forces became common sights near Thousand Thousand.<ref name="Geonosis" /> At some point before the end of the war, Makem Te rejoined the Galactic Republic to safeguard its mining sector. The Separatists stationed an experimental [[Tank/Legends|landtank]] called the ''[[Bogg Behemoth]]'' outside Thousand Thousand. The Republic deployed a [[Legion/Legends|legion]] of [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] led by the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] to defend the city and destroy the weapon before it could be made operational. The Republic's intelligence proved faulty, however, as the tank had already been brought online; during the ensuing [[Battle of Makem Te (Clone Wars)|battle]], the Republic forces destroyed the tank and captured its [[Engineer/Legends|engineer]], a [[Geonosian/Legends|Geonosian]] named [[Bogg]].<ref name="BTB">{{TCWComicCite|6.17|Burn the Behemoth!}}</ref> After the rise of [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] maintained deals brokered with the Separatists, but provided the caliphs with advanced weaponry and only kept occasional troops on Makem Te.<ref name="Geonosis" />

Despite the defeat of the Empire at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], the Council of Caliphs remained affiliated with various Imperial factions for nearly another 20 years. Imperial troops remained on Makem Te, making it a fortress world. However, after [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] forces allied with the New Republic won a [[Battle of Emmer (4 ABY)|battle]] at the nearby [[Emmer system/Legends|Emmer system]], Makem Te found itself isolated from other Imperial systems. In [[7 ABY/Legends|7 ABY]], the forces of the [[Warlord/Legends|Warlord]] [[Zsinj]] expanded [[Zsinj's Empire]] to include the Makem system, once again reuniting the Swokes Swokes with the Empire. The affiliation was short-lived, however, as Zsinj died in [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]], and his empire dissolved. The Swokes Swokes maintained their Imperial allegiances during the [[Thrawn campaign]], despite the fact that their world lay within the disputed [[Trans-Hydian/Legends|Trans-Hydian]].<ref name="TEA" /> When its final Imperial patron was vanquished, the caliphs remained neutral in galactic affairs and refused to join the New Republic.<ref name="Geonosis" />

By [[19 ABY/Legends|19 ABY]],<ref name="SA">[[Scourge (novel)|''Scourge'']], Acknowledgements</ref> the Congress of Caliphs had established diplomatic ties with the [[New Jedi Order]] on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]]. That year, Makem Te became a hub for the distribution of Tempest, a powerful form of spice that caused long-term users to fly into fits of murderous rage. The [[Pantoran/Legends|Pantoran]] [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Toro Irana]] became addicted to the substance and visited Makem Te to buy more. While waiting for a [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] [[drug dealer]] named [[Dejarro]] at a [[Unidentified Makem Te restaurant|restaurant]], Irana, high on Tempest, became embroiled in a brawl<ref name="Scourge" /> with [[Choka Chok]], the nephew of a [[Unidentified Swokes Swokes caliph|Swokes Swokes caliph]]. The encounter ended in not only Chok's death, but also that of five others, [[Dismemberment/Legends|dismemberment]] for twelve other Swokes Swokes, and Irana's own death after he misjudged his momentum and fell out a window.<ref name="Scourge" /> Afterward, the Congress of Caliphs complained to the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] about the incident, and Irana's [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]], the Human [[Jedi Archives/Legends|Jedi archivist]] [[Mander Zuma]], traveled to Makem Te to arrange Irana's [[Jedi funeral/Legends|funeral]] and to investigate the death. The search took the Jedi to a [[Unidentified Makem Te warehouse|warehouse]], where he came under attack by Rodians of the [[Bomu Clan]] and their Swokes Swokes minions. Zuma escaped with the help of Toro Irana's sister, [[Reen Irana]], and her [[Bothan/Legends|Bothan]] companion, [[Eddey Be'ray]]. The trio continued the investigation and followed the trail of the Tempest trade, which they endeavored to shut down. As their efforts bore fruit, the Bomu Clan slowly abandoned their spice dealings on Makem Te. Swokes Swokes addicted to the spice grew increasingly agitated as their supply was curtailed until only one dealer, a Rodian named [[Rolan (Human)|Rolan]], remained.<ref name="Scourge" />

During the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], the [[Yuuzhan Vong|invaders]] targeted Makem Te in an attempt to disrupt the Perlemian Trade Route. They bombarded the orbital fueling station, still in use since its creation millennia ago, and sent it crashing to the surface of the planet. It narrowly missed the Tract.<ref name="Geonosis" /> Years later, Makem Te fell within the bounds of the [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|Galactic Empire]] of [[Darth Krayt]].<ref name="TEA" />

==Swokes Swokes in the galaxy==
{{Quote|Brilliant! Such showmanship! Such panache! Such verve!|A Swokes Swokes dilettante, on [[Raal Yorta]]|<ref name="RR">''[[Rookies: Rendezvous]]''</ref>}}
[[File:SwokesSwokes.jpg|thumb|right|Oakie Dokes was an artist on Coruscant during the latter days of the Republic.]]
While many members of the species gained renown on their homeworld &mdash;such as influential importer and schinga breeder, [[Woorta Woorta]]; and the First Glorious Assassin of the Temple of the Beatific Razor, [[Fabswa]] the Mutilated&mdash; others emigrated. These often capitalized on their natural fighting abilities to find employment as [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguards]], [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]], and [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]].<ref name="Geonosis" /> For example, a Swokes Swokes was among the crew of the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] [[Reess Kairn]] sometime before [[27 BBY/Legends|27 BBY]].<ref name="TBH:AS">''[[The Bounty Hunters: Aurra Sing]]''</ref> Later, during the Clone Wars, the Swokes Swokes diplomat [[Mokshok]] found himself stranded near a [[Unidentified black hole|black hole]] in the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]] and joined the [[Black Hole Gang/Legends|Black Hole Pirates]] trapped there by its [[Gravity/Legends|gravity]] well. Mokshok became the first mate of the Human pirate [[Captain/Legends|captain]] [[Hethra Mcgrrrr/Legends|Hethra Mcgrrrr]] until the [[Trandoshan/Legends|Trandoshan]] [[Bossk/Legends|Bossk]] managed to usurp Mokshok's position.<ref name="BHP" /> Higher-ranking Swokes Swokes sometimes took up residence on out-of-the-way planets and became involved in organized crime.<ref name="Geonosis" /> Even [[Yeb Yeb Adem'thorn]], Makem Te's [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] during the last days of the Republic, was accused of corruption after he took up residence in an opulent abode on Coruscant.<ref name="Card-CCG-Yeb Yeb Adem'thorn">{{CCG|set=Coruscant Limited|cardname=Yeb Yeb Adem'thorn}}</ref>

Others tried to fit in with high society as [[Gambling/Legends|gamblers]] or dilettantes. [[Oakie Dokes/Legends|Oakie Dokes]] left her family's schinga ranch on Makem Te to show livestock on the galactic [[Capital/Legends|capital]] planet, [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. There, she mismanaged her funds and fell into poverty. She eventually discovered a talent for art&mdash;with works that necessitated the killing of her subjects.<ref name="DB Dokes" /> At least one Swokes Swokes was present at the [[Galaxies Opera House/Legends|Galaxies Opera House]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]] when Anakin Skywalker and [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] Palpatine were in attendance.<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref> By [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], [[Unidentified Swokes Swokes dilettante|another Swokes Swokes]] had clawed her way into high society on the planet [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]].<ref name="RR" />

On the desert world of [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], Swokes Swokes lived in [[Mochot Steep/Legends|Mochot Steep]]<ref name="SWR:O">''[[Star Wars: Outlander]]''</ref> and [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]].<ref name="TBH:AS" /> In the latter location, the Swokes Swokes [[Gragra/Legends|Gragra]] sold a variety of food items from a market stall,<ref name="JJJ">''[[Star Wars: Jar Jar's Journey Adventure Book]]''</ref> primary among them [[Gorg/Legends|gorgs]],<ref name="TPM" /> which she raised in the sewers beneath the town.<ref name="SWC:TP">''[[Star Wars Chronicles: The Prequels]]''</ref> [[Unidentified Swokes Swokes bartender|Another member of the species]] tended bar at Mos Espa's [[Poodoo Lounge]].<ref name="Podracing Tales">"[[Podracing Tales]]"</ref> Several Swokes Swokes worked in the nightlife establishments of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant's]] lower levels in the latter days of the Republic; such beings had difficulty telling a Human's age, so Human teenagers sometimes slipped into clubs illegally.<ref name="DSS" /> A Swokes Swokes was among the victims of the ruthless dictator [[Uda-Khalid]].<ref name="Survivors comic">{{Tales|13|Survivors (comic story)}}</ref>

A number of Swokes Swokes served in the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] and due to their lack of hair, Swokes Swokes [[Padawan/Legends|Padawans]] planted medallions into the flesh beneath their foreheads as an alternative to the standard [[Padawan braid/Legends|Padawan braid]] worn by apprentices.<ref name="tjp">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|But I have become oddly enamored with that Swokes Swokes. Sometimes, certain characters are just fun to draw.|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|<ref name="Blog-pablog|50">{{Blog|pablog|50|Rookies: Rendezvous -- Week Three Annotations}}</ref>}}
[[File:Swokes_Swokes_concept_art.jpg|thumb|Terryl Whitlatch's early concept sketch shows a Swokes Swokes as much plumper and less humanoid.|left]]
Artist [[Terryl Whitlatch]] designed the Swokes Swokes as one of the species for the Galactic Senate scenes of [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']].<ref name="Star Wars: Episode I Insider's Guide">[[Star Wars: Episode I Insider's Guide|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Insider's Guide'']]</ref> Whitlatch's concept art depicts the species as much fatter creatures with six [[Breast/Legends|breasts]]; short, pudgy legs, a plump body, and no clothing.<ref name="DBold">{{DB|character|gragra|Gragra|oldversion=20011229114830}} {{C|[https://web.archive.org/web/20011229114830/starwars.com/databank/character/gragra/img/bts_bg.jpg Archived image]}}</ref> The design was later used for Gragra the gorgmonger as well&mdash;a role that Whitlatch had originally conceived as being played by a [[Pacithhip/Legends|Pacithhip]].<ref name="The Art of Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace">''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace]]''</ref> Live Action Creature Effects Supervisor [[Nick Dudman]] named the species for his wife, [[Sue Oakes]], during the film's production.<ref name="DB-Gragra">{{DB|character|gragra|Gragra}}</ref><ref name="MOEI 67">''[[Star Wars: The Making of Episode I The Phantom Menace]]''</ref> The film, released in [[1999]], features the first appearance of the species, and its most prominent Swokes Swokes, Gragra, appears in several adaptations, including the [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|novelization]], [[Star Wars: Episode I — The Phantom Menace (comic series)|comic book]], and [[Star Wars Manga: The Phantom Menace|manga]]. The [[Alien/Legends|aliens]] have since appeared as background characters in the other prequel films and in various ''Star Wars'' comics. ''[[Podracing Tales]]'' ([[2000]]) and ''[[Rookies: Rendezvous]]'' ([[2006]]) feature two of the few Swokes Swokes characters with speaking roles.

A [[2003]] issue of ''[[The Official Star Wars Fact File]]'' presents the earliest history of the species. According to the ''Fact File'', the Clone Wars and the anti-alien policies of Emperor Palpatine caused the Swokes Swokes to all but disappear. The article suggests that they were little known throughout the galaxy during the New Order, their homeworld possibly destroyed<ref name="FF GOR1" /> or located far from major spacelanes. The ''Fact File'' then contradicts itself, claiming that as early as [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], the Swokes Swokes had gone largely unseen for at least a generation and that representatives such as Gragra may have been scouts or trailblazers.<ref name="FF GOR2" />

A starkly different background is detailed in the [[Wizards of the Coast]] roleplaying supplement ''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]'' ([[2004]]). This source adapted material originally written by [[Daniel Wallace|Dan Wallace]] in 1999 and 2000 for the canceled ''[[The Essential Guide to Episode I]]''.<ref name="Blog-danwallace|34">{{Blog|danwallace|34|Lostwords: The Essential Guide to Episode I}}</ref> In game terms, the book's Swokes Swokes are listed as being stronger and hardier than most species but less agile, clever, and likable.<ref name="Geonosis" /> Later sources, such as ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' ([[2008]]), support the Wizards of the Coast version of the species' background, so this is assumed to be the canonical one within [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]].

Even in Legends depictions, there are discrepancies in the Swokes Swokes' physiology. Both ''Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds'' and ''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]'' depict the aliens with large tails, but ''The Official Star Wars Fact File'' and the [[Hasbro]] action figure line show that the Gragra costume used in ''The Phantom Menace'' had no tail at all.<ref name="FF GOR4">{{FactFile|99|GOR 3-4|Gragra the Gorgmonger}}</ref><ref name="Hasbro" /> Similarly, the comic book ''[[The Bounty Hunters: Aurra Sing]]'' (1999) shows Swokes Swokes characters with different nostril and finger configurations than the aliens seen in the films and described by Wizards of the Coast. Likewise, the novel [[Scourge (novel)|''Scourge'']] by [[Jeff Grubb]] ([[2012]]) describes Swokes Swokes as having a "random" number of nostrils. These may be continuity errors, although it is possible that these are genetic variations, representations of subspecies, or illustrative of quirks in the Swokes Swokes' regenerative abilities.
